assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce a production sprite ATLAS for a 2D oblique Chinese historical strategy map. Reference image 1 is the approved Tongguan v5 art direction. Reference image 2 is the original pen-and-flat-color drawing reference. Match their casual expressive pen strokes with correct underlying structure, selective detail and very PALE muted colors. No polished rendering, no 3D shading, no ornate parchment, no micro-detail. The atlas itself must have a genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha background, not white, cream, grey or painted checkerboard. No labels, letters, numbers, border, grid lines, watermark, cast shadow, ground rectangle or full landscape. Each sprite is isolated from every other sprite with at least 10% empty margin inside its own cell. Do not let any stroke cross a cell boundary. Use a consistent fixed oblique map view. Draw complete silhouettes and don't crop any object.
Asset: ONE architectural atlas, square aspect ratio, ideally 1536x1536. Exactly 2 equal columns by 2 equal rows, FOUR complete isolated Chinese settlement sprites, centered individually with generous transparent gutters.
Upper left: CAPITAL. A large walled city with a broad high raised-platform imperial palace hall as dominant mass, correct supporting columns and stairs, a double-eaved roof, one subsidiary palace hall and low surrounding timber courtyard houses. One small Buddhist pagoda off to one side as a secondary landmark. Entire outer city wall closes correctly, two clear gatehouses. Palace mass visibly larger and taller than ordinary houses. Muted pale stone walls and brown-grey roofs.
Upper right: MEDIUM WALLED CITY. A coherent enclosing wall and gatehouses, irregular clusters of timber houses, two taller wooden halls and a single modest Buddhist pagoda; no imperial palace. Distinct outline and internal arrangement from capital.
Lower left: SMALL WALLED TOWN. Low enclosing wall, one principal gate, about six varied low timber buildings and one two-storey wooden house; clear simple courtyard spacing, no pagoda. Different silhouette from other cities.
Lower right: TONGGUAN GATE FORTIFICATION. A sturdy Chinese gatehouse with double-eaved roof on a correctly aligned masonry gate, short thick crenellated wall sections extending from its sides; the passage through the gate remains clearly visible. A compact pass barrier, not a complete city, with no attached mountain or landscape.
CRITICAL roof tile marks: hand-placed short strokes of visibly unequal lengths and spacings, some interrupted, some areas left unmarked. General stroke direction follows each roof plane. No perfect parallel barcodes, grid of tiles or perfectly repeated roof patterns. Structure remains accurate: walls connect, roofs align with buildings, platforms support halls, corners share perspective. Pale colors with slight warm timber accents, never saturated red/gold. Simple legible hand-drawn map miniatures, not detailed architectural illustrations. No words or city labels, no decorative land disks beneath them.
